reconcile.connective: Keil and Delitzsch resolve the two names by levirate marriage: Pedaiah fathered Zerubbabel on Shealtiel's childless widow, so the boy was entered as Shealtiel's legal heir.

discrepancy.connective: Isaac Asimov flags the divergence in his Guide to the Bible: Zerubbabel is "elsewhere ... listed as the son of another" (Shealtiel), left unreconciled.

excerpts.excerpt_text: But Shealtil also appears to have died without posterity, and simply to have left a widow, which necessitated a Levirate marriage on the part of one of the brothers (Deu 25:5-10; Mat 22:24-28). Shealtil's second brother Pedaiah appears to have performed his duty, and to have begotten Zerubbabel and Shimei by this sister-in-law (Ch1 3:19), the former of whom, Zerubbabel, was entered in the family register of the deceased uncle Shealtil, passing as his (lawful) son and heir, and continuing his family.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly explains how Zerubbabel can be both 'son of Pedaiah' (1 Chr 3:19) and 'son of Shealtiel' (Ezra/Neh/Hag/Matt/Luke): Pedaiah is the biological father via levirate marriage to Shealtiel's widow, Shealtiel the legal father by inheritance/register.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's catalog of 'apparent contradictions' resolved by loose father/son usage or alternate names names this passage directly: "Zerubbabel's father, 1 Chron. iii. 19 and Ezra iii. 2; Neh. xii. 1" (p. 352).
